title: Junta testing

problem.name: Junta testing
problem.statement_latex:
\textbf{Junta testing with membership queries.} Given $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ by a coherent membership oracle, distinguish functions depending on at most $k$ variables from functions at uniform Hamming distance at least $\varepsilon$ from every such function.

\textbf{Junta testing from quantum examples.} Distinguish $k$-juntas from functions $\varepsilon$-far from every $k$-junta using copies of $2^{-n/2}\sum_x|x,f(x)\rangle$. Classical access consists of independent uniform labeled examples.

\textbf{Distribution-free junta testing.} Given membership queries to $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ and sampling access to an unknown distribution $D$, distinguish $k$-juntas from functions with $\Pr_D[f(x)\ne g(x)]\ge\varepsilon$ for every $k$-junta $g$. The quantum model coherently accesses the specified oracles.

quantum.headline_latex: \textbf{Junta testing with membership queries.} $\Theta(\min\{2^{n/2},\sqrt{\log(2+\varepsilon 2^k)/\varepsilon}\})$ queries for $n\ge2k$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1/8$, by the optimal Boolean-junta tester. In the range $\varepsilon\ge2^{-k/16}$ this simplifies to $\Theta(\sqrt{k/\varepsilon})$.
quantum.details_latex:
\textbf{Junta testing from quantum examples.} $O(k/\varepsilon)$ quantum examples by Atici--Servedio Fourier sampling, testing whether observed Fourier supports fit within $k$ coordinates.

\textbf{Distribution-free junta testing.} $O(k/\varepsilon)$ queries by Belovs' distribution-free quantum junta tester.

classical.headline_latex: \textbf{Junta testing with membership queries.} $O(\min\{2^n,k\log k+k/\varepsilon\})$ classical queries by junta testing or truth-table acquisition, with $\Omega(k\log k)$ required at constant distance.
classical.details_latex:
\textbf{Junta testing from quantum examples.} Passive classical examples require a number growing with $n$, even for small fixed $k$; exhaustive empirical testing of all $k$-coordinate functions uses $O((k\log n+2^k)/\varepsilon^2)$ samples.

\textbf{Distribution-free junta testing.} $O((k/\varepsilon)\log(k/\varepsilon))$ adaptive queries by classical distribution-free junta testing, with an $\Omega(k\log k)$ lower bound at constant distance.
